The search turned up a handful of commonly recommended tab managers, though the sources vary in age and some are vendor-written.

- **Workona** is positioned as a workspace organizer that groups tabs into per-project spaces and syncs them. A Workona-authored review lists it at over 500,000 users, which is self-reported. Last updated: March 2024
- **Tab Manager Plus** is the most frequently recommended for quick searching. One listing describes it as quickly finding open tabs, seeing all windows in one view, finding duplicates and limiting tabs per window. A 2025 roundup gives it a 4.7/5 rating (1,059 reviews) and 200,000+ users.
- **Session Buddy** saves and restores whole sessions and collections, with search across saved sessions. One guide notes it can be a bit resource-intensive when managing large sessions.
- **OneTab** closes your open tabs and saves them as a group you can restore later. A Workona review describes it as a quick-cleanup option.
- **Aerys** is a simple option that shows all open tabs in a popup. Android Authority says it doesn't scale up super well and can get a bit crowded.
- **TooManyTabs** offers tab previews and suspension, and **Snoozz** suits people who use tabs as a to-do list. Both appear only in Workona's older reviews.

Two caveats. Chrome's native tab groups are a free alternative for lighter use; one review says they aren't quite as powerful as some dedicated tab managers. Also, several listings and roundups date from 2020–2023, so ratings and user counts may be out of date. I did not check the Chrome Web Store pages directly for current figures.

I couldn't build a reliable top 25. I got reliable data for one extension and a partial, unverified list for ten more.

**What blocked me**
- The Chrome Web Store search page loads results with JavaScript. My fetch tool got only the first 10 results. It showed no user counts or rating counts, and it can't click "Load more", so I couldn't go past page one.
- The same fetch tagged all 10 results as "Featured". I don't trust that, because the detail page I checked was the only one I could verify.
- The store doesn't sort by user count. A true top 25 would need user counts for every candidate, and I had no extension IDs to fetch the detail pages.

**Verified from its store detail page**

| Name | Users | Rating | Ratings | Last updated | Featured |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tab Manager Plus for Chrome | 200,000 | 4.4 | ~1.1K | Oct 15, 2026 | Yes |

**First 10 search results (ratings only, unverified)**

These are in search order, not ranked by users. Users, rating counts, update dates and Featured status are all unconfirmed.

| Name | Rating |
|---|---|
| Tab Manager by Workona | 4.2 |
| Tabs Manager | 3.3 |
| Tab Manager | 3.6 |
| Session Buddy - Tab & Bookmark Manager | 3.3 |
| Tab Manager v2 | 4.1 |
| Tab Session Manager | 3.5 |
| tabExtend - Easy Tab manager | 4.3 |
| Tab Manager Auto | 4.2 |
| Mark tab manager | 4.4 |
| Tab Manager Plus for Chrome | 4.4 |

A Workona-authored review claims "500,000+" users for Workona. That is self-reported and dated, so don't rely on it.

**Ways to get the full list**
1. I can fetch the detail page for each candidate. I'd need their store URLs or IDs, and I'd have to find those through more searches. I can do this for roughly 25 to 30 extensions, and it would take many fetches.
2. You open the store search in a browser, scroll to load more results, and paste the list or IDs to me. I'll fetch the exact figures for each.
3. A browser-automation setup, such as Playwright, could scrape the page with "Load more" clicked. I'd need to set that up.

Which would you like? Option 1 is the one I can start right away.

- [Chrome Web Store search: tab manager](https://chromewebstore.google.com/search/tab%20manager?itemTypes=EXTENSION)
- [Workona: Best Tab Manager Extensions for Chrome](https://workona.com/reviews/best-tab-manager-extensions-for-chrome)
